 About The Role
 We're hiring a senior, hands-on engineer who turns high-level concepts and architectural direction into production-grade software, with a high degree of autonomy. You will own microservices end to end: domain modeling, API design, implementation, and deployment and operation on Kubernetes.
The ideal candidate thinks like an architect but codes like a craftsman. You are comfortable debating trade-offs at the whiteboard, and just as comfortable turning those decisions into clean, testable,
 Job Responsibilities
Design and build microservices. Own services end to end with Java and Spring Boot: domain boundaries, API contracts (REST, gRPC, event-driven), data models and integration patterns. 
Turn architecture into implementation. Take high-level concepts and design decisions and turn them into concrete designs, working code and incremental delivery plans, with minimal hand-holding. 
Contribute to architecture. Evaluate alternatives, document decisions (ADRs), flag risks early, and push back constructively when a design won't hold up in production. 
Own the DevOps lifecycle. Containerize, deploy and operate services on Kubernetes. Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines, Helm charts or manifests, and infrastructure-as-code. 
Engineer for production. Design for scalability, resilience and observability: metrics, tracing, structured logging, health checks, graceful degradation and capacity planning. 
Raise the engineering bar. Lead by example through thorough code reviews, meaningful automated tests and pragmatic refactoring. Mentor mid-level engineers. 
Work across boundaries. Collaborate with product owners, architects, QA and other teams to clarify requirements, align on interfaces and deliver predictably. 
 Job Requirements
 Nice to have:
Experience with a major cloud provider (AWS, Azure or GCP) and managed Kubernetes (EKS, AKS, GKE). 
Observability tooling: Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, ELK or Loki. 
Infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, Pulumi) and GitOps tools (Argo CD, Flux). 
Service mesh (Istio, Linkerd) and API gateways.
